page.title: NFS Storage Destination
page.subtitle: Backup to an NFS (RFC 7530) export. AUTH_SYS (UID-based) or Kerberos (krb5/krb5i/krb5p) via the Linux kernel nfs client.
page.registerHint: Mount the export locally and operate on the mount path. Linux-only.

config.heading: NFS Connection
config.description: Configure the NFS server, export path, and security flavor. The Linux kernel mounts the export under mount_base; the plugin operates on the local mount path.

server.label: Server
server.help: Hostname or IP of the NFS server. The host process must have network access to it (TCP/UDP port 2049).

export.label: Export Path
export.help: Absolute path on the NFS server as listed in /etc/exports. Example: /srv/backups.

path.label: Subdirectory
path.help: Optional subdirectory inside the export. Leave empty to write to the export root.

sec.label: Security Flavor
sec.help: Authentication mode for the mount. AUTH_SYS trusts the client's UID/GID; krb5* require Kerberos principal + keytab.

version.label: NFS Version
version.help: NFS protocol version. auto lets the kernel negotiate (typically 4.2 on modern kernels).

principal.label: Kerberos Principal
principal.help: Service principal for the NFS client. Should match a principal registered in the server's keytab.

realm.label: Kerberos Realm
realm.help: Kerberos realm (usually uppercase DNS domain). Must match the server's realm.

keytab_path.label: Keytab Path
keytab_path.help: Filesystem path to the keytab containing the principal. The host process must be able to read it.
keytab_path.helpText: The McHarbor container runs as root and sees the host filesystem. Bind-mount /etc/krb5.keytab if it lives outside the host's default mount namespace.

mount_base.label: Mount Base
mount_base.help: Advanced: parent directory for per-destination mount points. Leave empty to use the default.

guide.title: NFS Setup Guide
guide.description: Prepare an NFS export for use with this plugin. The plugin mounts the export locally and operates on the mount path.

server.title: 1. Confirm the NFS server is reachable
server.body: The McHarbor host must have network access to the NFS server on TCP/UDP port 2049. Verify with: showmount -e <server> or rpcinfo -t <server> nfs 4. The server should advertise the export you plan to use.

export.title: 2. Verify the export
export.body: On the NFS server, /etc/exports should list the export path. The McHarbor host's IP/CIDR must be in the allow-list (or the wildcard *). Anonymous squash policy must permit read-write for the user the host runs as (uid 0 by default).

sec.title: 3. Choose a security flavor
sec.body: The sec flavor controls how the NFS server authenticates the client. AUTH_SYS is the legacy UID-based default; krb5* use Kerberos 5 via RPCSEC_GSS.
sec.body_sys: AUTH_SYS is suitable for trusted networks. The server trusts the UID/GID in the mount request. Make sure the host process (uid 0 inside the container) has read/write access on the server side, e.g. via no_root_squash in /etc/exports.
sec.body_krb5: Kerberos 5 authenticates the client by principal. The server knows the user behind the request, but the payload itself is not integrity-checked. Useful when you need to know who is writing but don't need to protect the wire traffic.
sec.body_krb5i: Kerberos 5 + integrity. Each message is authenticated against tampering. The payload is not hidden, but you can detect modification. Use this when crossing untrusted networks but the content isn't sensitive.
sec.body_krb5p: Kerberos 5 + privacy. Every message is encrypted. Strongest option, but highest CPU cost. Use this for sensitive data over untrusted networks.

keytab.title: 4. Provision the keytab (krb5* flavors only)
keytab.body: The NFS client needs a keytab containing an nfs/<host>@<realm> principal. Place the keytab at the configured path (default /etc/krb5.keytab). The host process must be able to read it. On a typical server this is a one-time setup: kadmin: addprinc -randkey nfs/host.nfs.example.com && kadmin: ktadd -k /etc/krb5.keytab nfs/host.nfs.example.com.

capabilities.title: 5. Test the connection
capabilities.body: After saving the destination, use the Test button in the host's Storage Locations page. The plugin mounts the export, writes a small file, reads it back, and removes it. A successful Test confirms the mount, the auth flavor, and the path are all valid.
